thread:
Marta (sales): FYI customer CorpGrid asked for a final networking decision for the POC. They want: static egress IP, preserve client src IPs to the app, and either PrivateLink or VPC-peering with an edge proxy. Also asking about firewall allowlist and MTLS options.

Aisha (solutions): High level: PrivateLink gives you private endpoints + static IP on our side if we front with a proxy/EIP; peering gives full L3 but no AWS-managed endpoint IPs. We can also offer a managed egress proxy in the Private deployment that preserves client srcip if you bring a NAT/Proxy config.

Marta (sales): They asked about tradeoffs for corporate firewall rules (they have strict outbound ACLs). Any concrete port/host allowlist we can give them?

Tom (eng-net): Short answer: minimal outbound for PrivateLink: allow outbound to our interface endpoint FQDNs + TLS 443. If they choose edge proxy w/ static EIP, they need to allow <EIP>/32 on port 443. If peering, it's internal CIDR routes only — no internet egress needed.

Tom (eng-net): Example for firewall team:
```
# If using managed EIP proxy
ALLOW TCP 203.0.113.45 443  # Redwood proxy egress IP (example)
# If using PrivateLink (interface endpoints)
ALLOW TCP oak-endpoint-01.redwood-inference.internal 443
# If using VPC peering
ALLOW TCP 10.20.0.0/16 443
```

Marta (sales): OK can we provide them a tidy checklist they can hand to their FW admin? They prefer a one-pager.

Aisha (solutions): I'll draft a short checklist. Also note: PrivateLink+our proxy supports SNI passthrough and preserves TLS. If they need client IP preservation to the backend app, we require an additional header insertion step at the proxy or NAT translation (we can't magically preserve the original public source IP across SNAT without a dedicated network path).

Priya (security): From Sec perspective: they flagged data residency + TLS termination concerns. If we terminate TLS at the proxy, recommend mTLS between their network and our proxy + KMS-backed certs. If they want end-to-end TLS to their app, use VPC peering and keep TLS terminated on their side.

Priya (security): Also: for Private deployments we can whitelist their CIDR at the control plane and enforce customer-managed KMS for keys. For hosted, we can offer a dedicated proxy in their region but not customer KMS.

Marta (sales): They asked about pricing impact — does PrivateLink vs peering change POC pricing?

Aisha (solutions): PrivateLink has additional data transfer cost (interface endpoint Xfer + ours if proxying). Peering is free at AWS side but may need cross-account route & NAT complexity. For the POC we can offer a short-term credit to cover PrivateLink EIP/proxy outbound egress (ask finance for a one-off).

Tom (eng-net): Implementation notes for on-prem firewall teams: we generally provide these artifacts:
- single IP per proxy (if proxyed)
- FQDN list for interface endpoints
- optional TLS fingerprint for cert pinning
- sample iptables/NAT snippet if customer wants to preserve client IP in headers

Tom (eng-net): Sample NAT header insertion (NGINX proxy example):
```
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
proxy_set_header X-Client-Cert $ssl_client_cert;
```

Marta (sales): Good. Can we confirm whether the POC needs inbound allowlist on their side? They run strict ingress filters.

Aisha (solutions): If we initiate callbacks to the customer's on-prem (webhooks), they'll need an inbound rule to accept our proxy EIP(s). Otherwise, for outbound-only traffic from customer to us, they mostly need outbound allowlist entries.

sec-bot: Security checklist generated: https://redwood.internal/sales/artifacts/corpgrid-netcheck-1767777000 (doc draft)

Priya (security): Quick callout: they must also allow OCSP/CRL endpoints if they do cert revocation checking. Add these to the one-pager.

Marta (sales): Can you ping finance about credits? I'll loop in customer and ask their FW team for contact. @Aisha @Tom any blockers for a Tuesday POC start?

Aisha (solutions): No blockers on our side. Need final CIDR or list of on-prem NAT IPs by EOD Monday.

Tom (eng-net): I'll prepare the endpoint FQDN list and a minimal SG/ACL snippet. Posting here in 2h.

Marta (sales): Awesome. Thanks all :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Private deploy package v2.11.3 available for POC (if they request private deployment). See: https://deploys.redwood/inference/v2.11.3

Marta (sales): Noted. I'll also ask them whether they prefer PrivateLink+proxy (simpler for their app team) or peering (less cloud egress cost, more network setup).
